person.name: Steven Davenport
person.text: Joined the Irish Film Board as **Inward Production Manager** and headed Screen Ireland's **Inward Production** department from 2016. He then relocated to **Los Angeles** to open Screen Ireland's **US office** as Head of US Production & Partnerships. Before that, **25 years as a line producer, production manager and location manager**. Film production diploma from **BCFE (Dublin)**. Regular speaker: AFCI Week LA, Whistler Film Festival (Ireland country of focus), Content LA, podcasts on filming in Ireland.

company.text: Fís Éireann/Screen Ireland is the State agency for the Irish screen industry (CEO **Désirée Finnegan**). It funds Irish film, TV drama and animation, promotes the 32% Section 481 tax credit to international productions and supports skills (Screen Skills Ireland). Its 2022 Sustainability Plan made a **carbon calculator mandatory** on all funded productions, launched a **Sustainability Advisor fund** and sustainability standards; funded live-action productions must engage a Sustainability Advisor and file emissions plans and reports. Big US titles shot in Ireland include Vikings: Valhalla and Bad Sisters.

financials.text: Government-funded agency, not a commercial company: no revenue or profit figures apply. What matters is that its **funding is conditional on sustainability reporting**, which creates demand for services like Flying Secoya's among the productions it supports.

industry.title: Film commissions now require green production
industry.text: Ireland, Northern Ireland and the UK tie public support to carbon tracking (Albert calculator, Screen Ireland calculator, Ecoprod's Carbon Clap). US productions shooting abroad must comply.

industry.title: US studios have their own ESG targets
industry.text: Studios and streamers report emissions and want consistent data across territories: one partner covering several countries helps.

industry.title: Calmer production market
industry.text: Steven has said the post-Covid production frenzy has calmed: Ireland competes harder on service, so a turnkey sustainability offer is a selling point.

talking_points: Which **US productions** coming to Ireland in 2027 will fall under the **mandatory sustainability standards**, and who helps them comply today?
Is there a **list of approved Sustainability Advisors / service providers** Screen Ireland shares with incoming productions? How does a provider get on it?
Would a **joint webinar or one-pager for US producers** (Shooting green in Ireland) be useful for his LA office?
How do US productions **reconcile Irish carbon reporting with their studio's own ESG reporting**? Secoset® can produce both.
Which **events** in LA (AFCI Week, Content LA, AFM) would make sense to meet in person?
